## Body

**Security: pass-with-notes**, round-three delta only, at `a8a5758702ce7208172f8af6d635c458dc754b43`, against `26d2df93dba7bb02dbaf7829928875c52d8961b3` (migration 0046).

S189-001 is closed for the scoped idle-holder nudge and its prime FYIs. The shared-occurrence race is removed for every iteration of the prime loop, not merely for the first prime. No new security finding was established in this delta.

## Closure

The holder nudge retains its own 16-byte OS-random part, minted before the stretch mark (`idle_nudge.rs:118-136,264-278`). Each prime-loop iteration now calls `occurrence()` again and constructs its FYI using only that independently minted value (`idle_nudge.rs:290-307`). It does not reuse the nudge part, an earlier prime's part or a value cached outside the loop.

The holder's ID and earlier `fyi.held` IDs remain observable as before, but none determines a later prime FYI's random part. The next part has not even been generated while an earlier identifying event is published. The only use of the new part is the corresponding `hold_fyi`; that path publishes its identifying held event after committing that row. Observing it then is too late to reserve it first.

This reasoning applies to any number of selected primes: every iteration repeats the fresh draw. It relies on `getrandom::fill` and ordinary 128-bit unpredictability, not a guarantee that independently random values can never collide.

The previous transactional conflicting-sender/recipient refusal and `fyi.refused` audit are untouched by this three-file delta. After a legitimate hold, an external caller cannot replace it as a different sender/recipient or obtain a false Held response. Same-sender/same-recipient retries still retain the original FYI. No new sender override, listener exposure, shell/path execution or C19/C21 disclosure is added.

## Failure and retained scope

A failed nudge draw still logs an error before marking. A prime FYI draw happens after the mark: failure holds nothing for that prime and records `error: ...` in its outcome/audit; the loop continues to other primes. This is fail-closed issuance of an ID, not durable retry of the spent notification attempt. No RNG-failure injection was executed or verified in CI.

The six other daemon FYI notice families still have their documented namespace exposure despite generic refuse-and-audit. The normal-message identity namespace is unchanged. They remain F141; this verdict is not global daemon-prefix protection or certification of every site's error handling.

Prior full-label cross-project fanout, cancellation/mark-before-send and failed-audit logging qualifications remain. The new identity repair does not add project-isolated labels, message-ownership enforcement or guaranteed delivery after failure.
